citations.description: Ticket 43ea comment: 'Recorded 2026-08-04. The operator running this session attested directly that all affected credentials in this incident have been rotated and all leaked material purged. ... The code prerequisite is satisfied and landed: 66af, commit 4e8c83c833, Gerrit change 1384, MERGED with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.' Scope note: 'The attestation above covers rotation and purge explicitly.' No deploy/container confirmation recorded.

findings.criterion: 66af code deployed to the prod box; running container confirmed to source the token from the X-Rebar-Token header and to carry TokenRedactingFilter (no `?token=` URL read).
findings.detail: The attestation comment (2026-08-04) names the code landing — commit 4e8c83c833, Gerrit change 1384, MERGED — but does not attest the deploy step: that the prod container was rebuilt from current main, restarted, and confirmed to be running with X-Rebar-Token header sourcing and TokenRedactingFilter active. The comment's own scope note says 'The attestation above covers rotation and purge explicitly,' implicitly acknowledging the deploy/container-confirmation step is not covered. No verifiable specific (deploy id, container image digest, observed log line, or console output) for the prod-box deploy is recorded.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment confirming the prod deploy: include the image rebuild timestamp or digest, the docker compose up -d run date/time, and an observed log line or `docker inspect` output showing the container is running the post-1384 image with X-Rebar-Token header sourcing and TokenRedactingFilter present.

citations.description: Ticket 43ea comment: 'all affected credentials in this incident have been rotated and all leaked material purged.' No mention of service-user.sh, SSM path, Gerrit HTTP password update, or webhooks.config push.

findings.criterion: Token rotated via service-user.sh: new value is the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, in SSM, and in the pushed webhooks.config; old (compromised) value no longer accepted.
findings.detail: The attestation says 'all affected credentials in this incident have been rotated and all leaked material purged' (2026-08-04, operator). This covers the fact of rotation but does not confirm the specific method (service-user.sh) or the three required sub-parts: (a) new value set as Gerrit HTTP password, (b) overwritten into SSM at /rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token, (c) substituted into webhooks.config and pushed to refs/meta/config. The AC explicitly requires all three sub-parts and the canonical tool; the attestation does not name any of them.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment confirming: (1) service-user.sh was run (or equivalent atomic steps), (2) the new token is set as the bot's Gerrit HTTP basic-auth password, (3) SSM parameter /rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token was updated (include the SSM put-parameter timestamp or version), and (4) webhooks.config was pushed to refs/meta/config (include the Gerrit change or commit id for that push). Also confirm the old token is no longer accepted.

citations.description: Ticket 43ea comment reviewed in full: no attestation of review-bot restart, inbound webhook test, or outbound LLM-Review vote with the new credential.

findings.criterion: review-bot restarted and verified: an inbound webhook/`/rerun` triggers a review AND an outbound LLM-Review vote lands with the new credential.
findings.detail: The attestation comment contains no mention of this end-to-end verification step. There is no recorded specific — no webhook trigger event, no /rerun invocation, no observed LLM-Review vote, no Gerrit change number showing a vote landed — that would substantiate this criterion. The comment covers rotation and purge, and the code landing, but is silent on the post-rotation functional verification.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment with: the docker compose up -d restart timestamp, a Gerrit change number (or /rerun invocation log) showing an inbound webhook triggered a review after rotation, and the resulting LLM-Review vote (+1 or otherwise) confirming outbound basic-auth works with the new credential.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
